and2.title: AND
and2.caption: The output is 1 only when both inputs are 1. Think of two switches in series: the current gets through only if both are closed.

or2.title: OR
or2.caption: The output is 1 when at least one input is 1. Two switches in parallel: either one on its own is enough.

not1.title: NOT
not1.caption: One input, one output, and the output is always the opposite. Also called an inverter.

nand2.title: NAND
nand2.caption: AND with the answer flipped. Note the bubble on the nose of the symbol: that bubble is the inversion.

nor2.title: NOR
nor2.caption: OR with the answer flipped. Output is 1 only when both inputs are 0.

xor2.title: XOR
xor2.caption: Exclusive OR: 1 when the inputs are different. The extra curved line at the back is what separates it from OR.

xnor2.title: XNOR
xnor2.caption: XOR with the answer flipped, so it is 1 when the inputs are the same. A one-bit equality test.

and3.title: Three-input AND
and3.caption: Three inputs means eight rows, and only the very last one gives a 1. Three inputs is the most the syllabus asks for.

or3.title: Three-input OR
or3.caption: Only the all-zeros row gives a 0. Every other row gives a 1.

demorgan-nand.title: NOT (A AND B)
demorgan-nand.caption: Invert the result of the AND.

demorgan-orNots.title: (NOT A) OR (NOT B)
demorgan-orNots.caption: Invert each input first, then OR them. Compare the output column with the one above: they are identical.

demorgan-nor.title: NOT (A OR B)
demorgan-nor.caption: Invert the result of the OR.

demorgan-andNots.title: (NOT A) AND (NOT B)
demorgan-andNots.caption: Invert each input first, then AND them. Again the output column matches the one above.

not-from-nand.title: NOT built from NAND
not-from-nand.caption: Tie both inputs of a NAND together and it behaves as an inverter.

and-from-nand.title: AND built from NAND
and-from-nand.caption: NAND then invert. The second NAND is wired as an inverter.

or-from-nand.title: OR built from NAND
or-from-nand.caption: Invert both inputs, then NAND them. This is De Morgan's law turned into hardware.

not-from-nor.title: NOT built from NOR
not-from-nor.caption: The same trick works for NOR.

xor-from-nand.title: XOR built from four NANDs
xor-from-nand.caption: Four NANDs and nothing else. Watch the propagation: the answer arrives three gate delays after the inputs change.

worked-ab-plus-c.title: F = A·B + C
worked-ab-plus-c.caption: Read it inside out: AND first, then OR. The diagram has the same shape as the expression.

worked-brackets.title: F = (A + B)·NOT C
worked-brackets.caption: Brackets change the order, so the OR happens before the AND. Compare this with the diagram above.

worked-alarm.title: House alarm
worked-alarm.caption: A is the alarm being armed, D the door sensor, W the window sensor. The siren sounds only when the alarm is armed and at least one sensor has tripped.

worked-majority.title: Majority vote of three
worked-majority.caption: Output is 1 when two or more inputs are 1. Used in safety-critical systems that run three copies of a computation and take the majority answer.

worked-unsimplified.title: Before simplification
worked-unsimplified.caption: Five gates and nine literals, straight from the truth table.

worked-simplified.title: After simplification
worked-simplified.caption: The same output column from four literals. Fewer gates means less silicon, less power and a shorter propagation delay.

half-adder.title: Half adder
half-adder.caption: Adds two single bits. S is the sum bit, C is the carry. 1 + 1 = 10 in binary, which is S=0 with C=1.

full-adder.title: Full adder
full-adder.caption: Two half adders plus an OR. The third input is the carry coming in from the column to the right, which is what lets these chain together into a full adder chain.

mux21.title: 2-to-1 multiplexer
mux21.caption: A selector. S picks which of the two data inputs reaches the output, like a railway points switch.

decoder24.title: 2-to-4 decoder
decoder24.caption: Exactly one output is 1 at a time, chosen by the two-bit number on A and B. This is how an address selects one memory row.

sr-latch.title: SR latch (NOR)
sr-latch.caption: Each gate feeds the other, so the circuit remembers. With S=R=0 the output stays where it was, which is why 'x' appears rather than a fixed 0 or 1.

static-hazard.title: A static-1 hazard
static-hazard.caption: With B=1 and C=1 the output should stay at 1 whatever A does. Slow the clock right down and step through: the output dips to 0 for one gate delay as A falls, because the inverter arrives late.
